section: How much prilocaine is too much?
sentence_as_it_stands: The stricter figure: [dose figure omitted]. The one published analysis that contradicts Guay contradicts it downwards. Schmittner and colleagues (2010) measured methemoglobin after high-dose prilocaine infiltration of skin and concluded that because the concentrations reached are unpredictable, prilocaine infiltration should be limited to [dose figure omitted].
quote: Current publications recommend a dose limitation of [dose figure omitted].8 … As a result of possible and unpredictable high MHb concentrations, TLA can only be recommended with prilocaine in doses of [dose figure omitted].8
corrected_wording: Schmittner and colleagues (2010), a prospective study of systemic cytokines in 30 patients given high-dose tumescent (subcutaneous) prilocaine for large skin resections, measured methaemoglobin serially and found it unpredictable between patients; the limit in their conclusion is the general limit Guay's own summary concludes with, and they cite Guay for it, so it repeats Guay's conclusion rather than contradicting it.
notes: Same point as the C071 own-question update, recorded for its place in the body text. Reference 8 is Guay 2009; Schmittner cites it five times. The paragraph just above on the same page already says "Guay's closing recommendation is to hold to [dose figure omitted] generally", so the page contradicts itself; the section's opening line ("the better-sourced the number, the lower it is") also leans on Schmittner as a separate, lower source. Also: the route was subcutaneous tumescent infusion rather than 'infiltration of skin', and methaemoglobin was the presumed mediator in a cytokine study. The paper found no correlation between applied dose and methaemoglobin, so the limit is adopted from Guay, not derived from its data. Page fetched in full (no truncation markers).

section: Sources › Systemic toxicity and methemoglobin (Schmittner entry)
sentence_as_it_stands: This is the only paper that cites Guay contrastingly, and it argues for a lower ceiling, not a higher one.
quote: As a result of possible and unpredictable high MHb concentrations, TLA can only be recommended with prilocaine in doses of [dose figure omitted].8
corrected_wording: Schmittner cites Guay five times and attributes the limit it adopts to Guay; that limit is the general one Guay's summary concludes with — lower than the adult figure in Guay's results, not lower than Guay's own conclusion.
notes: Ambiguous rather than plainly wrong, hence low: if 'a lower ceiling' means lower than the adult figure this page treats as Guay's, it is literally true; if it means Schmittner disagrees with Guay, it is not, since Schmittner cites Guay for the figure. 'Cites Guay contrastingly' reflects a citation-database label that could not be checked (the Scite connector requires a paid plan); the page's own Guay entry records '3 supporting, 3 contrasting', which fits 'the only paper' only if all three statements are Schmittner's (it cites Guay in five sentences; the Introduction sentence setting Guay's recommendation against larger amounts used by others is the likeliest to be labelled contrasting). The rest of the entry is accurate ('the primary outcome was cytokine levels, not methemoglobin, and the sample is small'; volume, pages and DOI correct). Same point as C071.

section: Why the prilocaine ceiling is methaemoglobinaemia and not milligrams
sentence_as_it_stands: A stricter line than [dose figure omitted] has been published, and it comes from a different body of work. The study of high-dose tumescent prilocaine infiltration of skin recommends holding to [dose figure omitted] — [dose figure omitted] — because the methaemoglobin concentrations reached are unpredictable, and the 242-episode summary reaches the same [dose figure omitted] as its own closing general recommendation, having set [dose figure omitted] for children over six months. Two bodies, two numbers, and the lower one is [rest of sentence omitted: dose figures and planning advice]
quote: Current publications recommend a dose limitation of [dose figure omitted].8 … As a result of possible and unpredictable high MHb concentrations, TLA can only be recommended with prilocaine in doses of [dose figure omitted].8
corrected_wording: Both numbers come from the 242-episode summary: a figure for adults in its results and a lower general limit in its conclusion. Schmittner 2010, a cytokine study after high-dose tumescent prilocaine, adopts the concluding limit and cites the summary for it; it did not derive a limit from its own data, in which applied dose and methaemoglobin were not correlated.
notes: The page presents the stricter line as reached independently by 'a different body of work' ('Two bodies, two numbers'). In Schmittner's text the limit is what 'current publications recommend', cited to Guay (reference 8), and the closing recommendation cites Guay again; every patient received amounts far above that limit, and the paper reports 'no statistically significant correlation between the applied doses of prilocaine and MHb' (PDF page 4), so its own data show only that methaemoglobin after large doses was unpredictable. The numbers on the page do not change; their provenance is one source, not two. In sentence_as_it_stands the body-weight conversion that follows the limit is folded into one omitted figure. No figure is proposed here. Same point as C071/D075.

sentence_as_it_stands: Limits: the primary outcome was cytokine levels, not methaemoglobin, and the sample is small; it is the only paper that cites the 242-episode summary contrastingly, and it argues for a lower ceiling, not a higher one.
quote: Current publications recommend a dose limitation of [dose figure omitted].8
corrected_wording: Limits: the primary outcome was cytokine levels, not methaemoglobin, and the sample is small (30 patients); it cites the 242-episode summary for the limit it adopts, which is that summary's own concluding limit.
notes: Second place the C071 point appears; this is the sentence tested as D075. Ambiguous, hence low: the same page's Guay entry says the summary's 'own closing general recommendation is the stricter [dose figure omitted]', so 'a lower ceiling' can only mean lower than the adult threshold; read as disagreement with the summary it is wrong. section: Who is at extra risk, and what should be watched for?
sentence_as_it_stands: Vasters and colleagues (2005) gave [dose figure omitted] of prilocaine to 162 patients for nerve blocks before knee surgery and measured methemoglobin three hours later.
